findings.charge: The v8 artifact self-labels as v7. basedOn.predecessorV6.role retains, byte-for-byte from leftover-join.v7, the sentence 'This v7 remasures occupancy v1 stale after occupancy v2 (D-219).' In v7 that sentence was a correct speaker self-reference; carried unchanged into an artifact whose artifact field is 'platform-tcb-leftover-join.v8' and whose version is 8, it makes the document attribute its own remasuring act to a different, frozen artifact. This is the leftover predecessor-role sentence the dispatch names as an attack vector.
evidence: The subject contains exactly three 'This v<N>' speaker self-labels. Two read 'This v8' (basedOn.predecessorV7.role, findingDisposition[0].disposition). The third reads 'This v7' (basedOn.predecessorV6.role). 'This v<N>' is used nowhere in this lineage except as a speaker self-reference, so the label is unambiguous in context.

It is a verbatim carry, not a deliberate historical statement. Live v7's basedOn.predecessorV6.role and live v8's are string-equal: 'Predecessor. Unmoved. Dual ACCEPT 0/0. Recorded as current DR-126 leftover-join. Cited occupancy v1 as the specification. This v7 remasures occupancy v1 stale after occupancy v2 (D-219). Not this artifact's version number.'

The full v7->v8 field diff shows ten changed scalars. The author did advance the speaker label everywhere else it appears, including the closely parallel parentReview.role ('not leftover-join.v6' -> 'not leftover-join.v7') and findingDisposition[0].disposition ('This v7 does not re-land it' -> 'This v8 does not re-land it'). basedOn.predecessorV6.role is the one site the sweep missed.

The sentence is now false as written on its own terms. v8's purpose and authorityClaim both state that v8 is the remasuring speaker ('v8 remasures leftover-join.v7 after CLAUDE-PTLJ-V7-SF1'), and predecessorV7.role states 'This v8 lands CLAUDE-PTLJ-V7-SF1'. The document therefore contradicts itself about which artifact is speaking.

This is the named recurring defect of this lineage, not a novel one. The subject's own basedOn.predecessorV4.role records the identical failure mode one iteration earlier: v4 'Set version 4 but retained the v2 predecessor-role sentences.' basedOn.predecessorV3.role records the sibling identity defect: 'artifact ...v3 with version 2.' Both were charged as CLAUDE-PTLJ-V3-SF1 at SHOULD-FIX.

The carry was predicted. The live v7 Stage A review (11b08b19), in CLAUDE-PTLJ-V7-SF1's whyThisIsNotPedantry, states the error 'will carry into v8 the way the "does not reuse" sentences carried from v2 into v4.' The disposition sentence itself was repaired; its untouched sibling in predecessorV6.role carried.
findings.whyThisIsNotPedantry: CLAUDE-PTLJ-V3-SF1 and CLAUDE-PTLJ-V7-SF1 were both sustained on the ground that this lineage misstates its own custody in the very fields that record custody, and that a later reader keying on those fields would be misled. basedOn.predecessorV6.role is exactly such a field: it is where a reader learns which artifact remasured occupancy v1 as stale. Recording that act to 'This v7' assigns it to a frozen, split, CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED artifact that the same document elsewhere declares is not current — while v8, the artifact actually performing the remasurement, goes uncredited in that sentence. The defect is also self-propagating in the demonstrated way: the same sentence has now survived one full REJECT-and-repair cycle untouched, and on the v2->v4 precedent it will survive into v9 unless it is named.
whyNotABlockerOrMustFix: No measurement is corrupted. All 29 inline pairs, all 29 recordedInputs entries and file08Pin measure equal to live bytes; zero mismatches.

leftoverDesign remains [OBL-G22-FX-AUTHORING, OBL-RESERVED-TABLES] and the obligations block is byte-identical to v7's; required-now stays 28; no register cell, gate, table, selector or fixture is touched; binds NOTHING; Class A stays unopened.

The substantive claim inside the sentence is true of v7 and remains true of v8 — occupancy v1 is stale after occupancy v2 (D-219). Only the speaker attribution is wrong, and the identity fields artifact and version are themselves correct at v8.
The dispatch's protected repairs all hold: CLAUDE-PTLJ-V7-SF1 is landed, CLAUDE-PTLJ-V3-SF1 is attributed to v5 and not re-landed.
findings.repair: Advance the speaker label in basedOn.predecessorV6.role to the speaking artifact, e.g. '... Cited occupancy v1 as the specification. This v8 remasures occupancy v1 stale after occupancy v2 (D-219). Not this artifact's version number.' If the intent was instead to record that v7 was the first artifact to perform that remasurement, state it as predecessor history rather than as a speaker self-label — 'leftover-join.v7 first remasured occupancy v1 stale after occupancy v2 (D-219); this v8 carries that remasurement forward' — so no sentence in a v8 document opens with 'This v7'. Consider adding a lineage rule to the successor: no 'This v<N>' string may survive an increment unless N equals the top-level version field, which would have caught this, CLAUDE-PTLJ-V3-SF1 and the v4 carry mechanically.
